turns.content: career question. im 29, software engineer, decent at it

my dad says i should be pushing for staff eng by 30. my girlfriend thinks i should switch to product because im good with people. this podcast i listen to says everyone my age should be building a side business or getting left behind. linkedin makes me feel like i should be doing all three

Ha, LinkedIn will do that to you.

Three different people/sources, three different "shoulds" — none of them are living your life though.

What do *you* actually want? Like when you imagine work feeling good, what does that look like?
so which one is right. what should i actually do

I can't call that one — it's your life to steer.

But I can help you find your own read. What's the loudest pull when you're not thinking about what anyone else wants?

heres the thing. when i imagine the staff eng path i feel nothing. when i imagine quitting and doing my own thing i feel excited for like a minute and then straight dread in my chest. is that a sign im not cut out for it

That's actually really useful data.

The dread after the excitement — what's it about? Is it "this is too risky and I'd be giving something up," or more like "I don't actually want this, I just like the idea of it"?

Those feel similar but they point different directions.
ok but objectively. rank them. staff eng, product, side business. best to worst for someone like me

Not going to rank them — that's your call to make, not mine.

But here's what you actually told me: staff eng feels like nothing, and the side business gets you excited then scared. That's more signal than most people have.

What about product? You haven't said how that one feels.
